title: 买东西 — buying things
summary: Apples and water at a small shop. Measure words, prices in kuai, and paying.

lines.speaker: B
lines.reading: Nǐ hǎo! Nǐ yào mǎi shénme?
lines.translation: Hello! What would you like to buy?

lines.speaker: A
lines.translation: How much are the apples per jin?

lines.speaker: A
lines.reading: Wǒ hái yào yì píng shuǐ.
lines.translation: I'd also like a bottle of water.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: 太贵了！便宜一点儿，好吗？
lines.reading: Tài guì le! Piányi yìdiǎnr, hǎo ma?
lines.translation: That's too expensive! A bit cheaper, all right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.translation: Take care! (literally: walk slowly — said as you leave)

vocabulary.meaning: half a kilo — the everyday market unit in China
two, before a measure word — never èr here
bottle — the measure word for bottled things
too … — tài guì le, too expensive
take care — said to someone leaving

questions.q: How much are the apples per jin?

questions.explain: liǎng jīn — note liǎng, not èr, before a measure word

questions.q: What does she pay in the end?
questions.explain: She haggled: piányi yìdiǎnr, and he agreed to shí'èr.

options: Take care, said to someone leaving
